transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-27
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (MedPrime CTO), Laura Martinez (MedPrime Head of DS), Sofia Alvarez (PM), Tom Reed (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining. um we're gonna run through the poc scoping and specifically the quality eval plan that priya put together. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Daniel: good, thanks. excited to get this scoped. we have a pretty tight timeline, quarter end push.
[00:12] Laura: yep, want to make sure accuracy and hallucination rates are measured.
[00:16] Priya: great — i'll share my screen in a sec. quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, golden prompts, regression tests, scoring approach, and timelines. crosstalk ok?
[00:26] Sofia: yep fine.
[00:28] Priya: (screen) so first success criteria suggested: 1) factual accuracy >= 95% on key clinical entities, 2) hallucination rate < 2% on critical fields, 3) format fidelity 99% for EHR import fields, 4) latency SLA <= 700ms p50 for single threaded runs. these are placeholders we can calibrate.
[00:44] Laura: the 95% is on entity extraction or generated summary?
[00:47] Priya: good call — for generated clinical summaries our split is: NER/entity correctness target 95%, overall summary factuality target 90% by combined human+automated checks. we flagged critical fields (meds, dosages, diagnoses) as higher weight.
[01:04] Marcus: also recommend measuring format fidelity separately — so the downstream ETL doesn't break. we use deterministic format checks and schema validation.
[01:12] Tom: on security we need retention policy and KMS for keys, plus audit logs. also will need SOC2 artifact.
[01:18] Jordan: noted, tom. we'll include SOC2 and the security pack. tom, can you confirm minimal KMS setup?
[01:22] Tom: yes will confirm, i'll send requirements by next week.
[01:26] Priya: next workload sizing: Laura, can you confirm average note length and peak concurrent users?
[01:31] Laura: avg 420 tokens per note, 95th percentile 1,600 tokens. about 1200 notes/day initially, peak concurrency ~30 simultaneous analysts hitting API during batch windows.
[01:42] Priya: ok that maps to our test footprint. for POC we typically run 500 samples with synthetic load to emulate concurrency; for a performance bench we'll do 10k tokens per second sustained bursts to see batching impact.
[01:54] Daniel: timeline wise we want POC start week of 3/10 and wrap in 3 weeks, is that doable?
[01:58] Jordan: yes that's tight but doable if artifacts are delivered on schedule.
[02:02] Priya: benchmark plan: two tracks — functional quality and perf/econ. For quality: we will create a golden set of prompts + expected outputs (golden prompts spreadsheet link - https://redwood.example/golden-prompts (note: link is placeholder)). we'll run automated scoring (ROUGE/EM/precision/recall on extracted entities) plus human review for a random sample.
[02:22] Sofia: for the golden outputs, do you need exact phrasing or tolerant matching?
[02:26] Priya: prefer tolerant matching for prose (semantic similarity) and exact matching for structured fields. we'll annotate which fields require exactness.
[02:33] Priya: regression tests: every model update or tuning run will be run against the golden set. we'll flag any regressions beyond x% (configurable). also we recommend hallucination checks: negative prompts and contradiction detection plus question-answer based factuality tests.
[02:48] Marcus: note: KV cache was spelled out as K-V cache in doc but sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" in transcripts — minor typo in generated artifacts, we'll standardize.
[02:58] Laura: scoring approach? how do you weigh automated vs human?
[03:01] Priya: our suggested approach: primary automated score 70% (entity F1, schema pass rate, format fidelity) + 30% human rating on 200-sample stratified by clinical note type. human rubric covers accuracy, missing critical info, hallucination, and readability.
[03:18] Daniel: i want to make sure hallucination detection covers invented medications or dosages — that is non-negotiable.
[03:24] Priya: agreed — we give meds/dosage fields higher weight and add contradiction QA steps to detect invented entries.
[03:30] Jordan: on model variants, we'll test two families: a high-accuracy larger model and a faster quantized variant; fallback policies if latency spikes. cost/perf tradeoffs will be in the economic bench.
[03:44] Laura: can we have a pass/fail gating for go/no-go? like if hallucination > 2% on critical fields we stop.
[03:49] Priya: yes we will codify gating criteria in the SOW. Gate thresholds: hallucination on critical fields <=2%, entity F1 >= 0.95, format fidelity >=99%.
[03:59] Marcus: for perf tests we'll simulate 30 concurrent clients, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost per 1k tokens; also test dedupe/prefix caching to see cost impact.
[04:12] Sofia: timeline and responsibilities recap?
[04:14] Jordan: action items we've captured: jordan will send SOW and pricing by 3/3; priya will share golden prompts template and eval spreadsheet by 2/28; laura to upload 500 de-identified notes by 3/7; tom to confirm KMS and SOC2 items by 3/5.
[04:31] Tom: will get SOC2 artifacts, but might need an NDA side channel, is there a place to upload?
[04:36] Jordan: yes we'll share secure S3 link and a minimal NDA if needed.
[04:40] Laura: QA on the scoring — can you show an example rubric?
[04:44] Priya: sure, quick example: entity F1 calculation, format pass/fail, hallucination boolean per sample, human score 1-5 across four axes. combined score = 0.7*auto + 0.3*(human_mean/5). we'll include thresholds.
[04:59] Daniel: sounds good. any concerns about PII in samples? we only will upload de-identified notes.
[05:04] Jordan: perfect. we'll also support private deployment options for stronger data controls if needed later.
[05:08] Laura: ok final question — how often will regression tests run, on every model change?
[05:12] Priya: for POC we'll run them on every tuned checkpoint and before any rollout. in production we recommend nightly runs for regressions and alerts on threshold breaches.
[05:22] Jordan: wrap up — next steps and recap. we'll send SOW and links, you send sample notes and security reqs. schedule bench week of 3/10. any other blockers?
[05:33] Daniel: none from me. thanks all.
[05:36] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email. bye.
